headline: Bangladesh to field first against Australia in opening Test after 23 years in Darwin
summary: Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto lost the toss, marking Bangladesh's first Test match on Australian soil since 2003.
details: Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto lost the toss and was asked to field first in the opening Test of the two-match series against Australia. The match is being held at Marrara Stadium in Darwin on Thursday, marking Bangladesh's return to Test cricket in Australia after 23 years.

The Tigers previously played a Test series in Australia in 2003, just three years into their Test journey, losing both matches by an innings in Darwin and Cairns. This current series presents a significant challenge against an Australian side that currently leads the World Test Championship standings.

Bangladesh's XI features a balanced attack with three pacers – Taskin Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, and Ebadot Hossain – and two spinners, Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Taijul Islam. The batting order sees Tanzid Hasan and Shadman Islam opening, followed by Mominul Haque at three and captain Shanto at four.

Experienced campaigner Mushfiqur Rahim will play his first Test in Australia in his 21-year international career. Litton Das, who made a remarkable recovery from injury, has also been included in the XI, batting at six and taking wicket-keeping duties after passing a fitness test.

Australia's lineup includes a strong batting order with Travis Head and Jake Weatherald opening, followed by Marnus Labuschagne and Steven Smith. Their formidable pace attack is led by Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, and Josh Hazlewood, with Nathan Lyon as the sole spinner.

Bangladesh will need to perform exceptionally to make this tour memorable, especially after suffering an innings-and-38-run defeat to a Cricket Australia XI in their only tour match. The team was bowled out for just 54 in the second innings of that match, highlighting areas for improvement in both batting and bowling.

headline_marked: [[Long load shedding hits various Dhaka areas at night]], causing discomfort amid heat
headline: Long load shedding hits various Dhaka areas at night, causing discomfort amid heat
summary: Residents reported power outages lasting over an hour in several areas, including Bashundhara, Eskaton Garden, and Mohammadpur, causing significant discomfort in the sweltering heat. This widespread disruption is attributed to the ongoing gas crisis affecting
details: Widespread load shedding occurred in various areas of Dhaka on Wednesday night, with power outages lasting over an hour in many locations, including Bashundhara R/A, Eskaton Garden, Kazipara, and Mohammadpur. Residents faced significant discomfort due to the prolonged power cuts amid the sweltering heat.
Residents from areas such as Karwan Bazar, Panthapath, and West Rajabazar reported outages between 9 PM and 1:30 AM. A reporter in Sheorapara experienced a power cut for nearly an hour around 11 PM.

A Mouchak resident noted that while transformer issues usually resolve within 5-10 minutes, power did not return for almost 50 minutes on Wednesday night. Anika Tasnim from Bashundhara R/A stated she had not experienced such long midnight load shedding in Dhaka before, despite receiving double electricity bills.

Rahat Ahmed, a journalist and Kazipara resident, described Wednesday night's outage as the longest in his area in three years. He highlighted the difficulty of sleeping due to intense heat and mosquitoes, urging the government to improve electricity management for public relief.

The situation was not uniform across the capital, with some areas like Mirpur-11 and Journalist Plot experiencing normal supply until late night. However, a resident noted an outage in the Bihari Camp area around 10:30 PM.

Nationwide load shedding has increased due to an ongoing gas crisis, which has significantly reduced power generation. On Wednesday, the maximum load shedding reached 3,382 megawatts across the country.

Data from the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) and Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB) show peak load shedding figures: 3,671 MW on Sunday, rising to 3,757 MW on Monday, then 3,465 MW on Tuesday, and 3,382 MW on Wednesday. On August 11 at midnight, total load shedding nationwide was 3,592 MW, with REB areas alone accounting for 3,34 MW.

Gas supply has also decreased, with only 203 crore cubic feet available yesterday against a demand of 380 crore cubic feet. Adverse weather in the sea has reduced gas supply from Summit's floating LNG terminal to below 10 crore cubic feet.

State Minister for Power, Energy, and Mineral Resources, Anindo Islam Amit, told Prothom Alo on Wednesday that gas supply shortages are disrupting electricity production. He assured that the government is making maximum efforts to improve the power and gas situation.
